--- title: "Sensitivity analyses" --- ## Model status and overall results The three prespecified sensitivity analyses were run for each of the seven moderators included in the primary model set. The table below is generated from the synced model summaries rather than entered by hand. A changed coefficient is one whose sign or 95% credible-interval conclusion differs from its matched primary-model coefficient; intercepts are excluded from this count. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Sensitivity-model availability, stability, and diagnostics.
Analysis Models available Changed coefficients Max Rhat Divergences Status
Minimum total sample size (nb + nb b % 40) 7 8 of 36 1.010 58 complete
No phylogenetic random effect 7 3 of 36 1.009 0 complete
Study-system (sys_id) random effect 7 7 of 36 1.009 33 complete
````` ::: ::: All 21 expected sensitivity models have cached results. Removing the phylogenetic random effect produced the fewest changes relative to the primary fits. The minimum-sample-size and study-system analyses produced more changes, and their divergent transitions mean those differences should be interpreted alongside the model-specific diagnostics rather than as definitive reversals. ## Detailed results The appendices report every location and scale coefficient beside the matched primary estimate, together with convergence diagnostics: - [Minimum total sample size (N >= 40)](appendix/sensitivity_min_n.qmd) - [No phylogenetic random effect](appendix/sensitivity_no_phylogeny.qmd) - [Study-system (`sys_id`) random effect](appendix/sensitivity_sys_id.qmd) Highlighted rows in those tables identify coefficients whose sign or credible-interval conclusion changes. The detailed tables use raw treatment-coded coefficients so that each sensitivity estimate is compared like-for-like with the corresponding primary fit.
